title: Bacterial Transformation, Inoculation, and Glycerol Stock
author: Jeffery T Jolly
materials: Determine the appropriate chemically competent E. coli strain for your DNA type (e.g., cloning, lentiviral, recombinant protein expression, or Gateway cloning). Explanation: Different strains have genetic modifications that optimize transformation efficiency or plasmid stability for specific applications. Bacterial Strain Selection Guide: One Shot Mach1 T1 (ThermoFisher, C862003) Primary Purpose / Strengths: • Extremely rapid growth (colonies visible ~8 h)• High transformation efficiency (> 1×10⁹ cfu/µg)• Phage-resistant (T1/T5• Blue-white screening• Reduced recombination• Enhanced plasmid yield Recommended Use: Fast turnaround cloning; ideal when time-sensitive, high yield, phage resistance, and screening are priorities. One Shot TOP10 (ThermoFisher, C404003) Primary Purpose / Strengths: • Very high transformation efficiency (> 1×10⁹ cfu/µg)• Broad cloning utility• Compatible with methylated DNA• Blue-white screening Recommended Use: Standard cloning workflows, library construction, or work with genomic/methylated inserts. DH5α (available from multiple vendors, e.g., Invitrogen, NEB) Primary Purpose / Strengths:• High transformation efficiency• recA1 and endA1 mutations improve plasmid maintenance and purity• Supports blue-white screening via lacZΔM15 Recommended Use: Routine cloning requiring high plasmid yield and purity, such as sequencing or subcloning. BL21(DE3) (ThermoFisher protein expression strains) Primary Purpose / Strengths: • Optimized for recombinant protein expression via T7 system• Lacks major proteases (Lon, OmpT) for higher yields Recommended Use: Protein expression from T7-promoter constructs, large-scale or high-yield production. XL1-Blue / BW3KD (BW3KD info – PMC article) Primary Purpose / Strengths: • XL1-Blue: robust general cloning strain• BW3KD: extremely high transformation efficiency, ideal for large-fragment DNA assembly Recommended Use: XL1-Blue for standard cloning; BW3KD for complex assembly or large plasmid work.

steps.title: Prepare Equipment and Cells
steps.instruction: Prepare the heat block and competent cells for transformation.

substeps.instruction: Set the heat block to 42 °C.
Thaw a tube of competent cells on ice for 7 minutes.

steps.title: Transform Competent Cells
steps.instruction: Introduce plasmid DNA into the competent cells.

substeps.instruction: Add the desired amount of plasmid DNA (1 pg - 100 ng) to a 50 µL aliquot of competent cells; the volume of DNA must not exceed 3 µL (0.5 µL is typically optimal).
If transforming post LR reaction or if contaminants/salts are present, dilute the product 1:1-1:5 with DI water.
Flick the tube gently to mix; do not pipette up and down.
Incubate the DNA–cell mixture on ice for 7 minutes.

steps.title: Heat Shock and Recovery
steps.instruction: Perform heat shock to induce DNA uptake and allow cells to recover.

substeps.instruction: Heat-shock the cells at 42 °C for 40 seconds.
Quickly place the cells back on ice for 7 minutes.
Add 300 µL SOC medium (or clean terrific broth) to the cells and gently resuspend by pipetting.
Incubate on a warm shaker at 37 °C, 300-500 rpm for 1 hour.

steps.title: Plate Transformed Cells
steps.instruction: Plate the recovered cells onto selective agar for colony growth.

substeps.instruction: Warm TB + antibiotic agar plates at 37 °C.
If using the over-agar method for antibiotics: dilute antibiotic stock 1:100 with LB/TB medium, apply 150 µL evenly to the plate surface, and allow 30 minutes for absorption.
Spread 300 µL of transformed culture onto the plate (alternatively, split 250 µL on one plate and 50 µL on another).
Incubate plates upside down at 37 °C overnight.
Collect colonies 18-24 hours after plating.
Wrap plates in parafilm to prevent drying.
Store plates upside down at 4 °C if using within a week.

steps.title: Inoculate Liquid Culture
steps.instruction: Grow a liquid culture from a single colony.

substeps.instruction: Prepare 14 mL culture tubes.
Add 3-7 mL Terrific Broth (TB) and 3-7 µL/mL antibiotic (1:1000 dilution from -20 °C stocks) to each tube.
Pick a single colony with a sterile pipette tip, drop it into the tube, and vortex to disperse.
Loosen the caps on the 14 mL tubes to allow gas exchange.
Incubate at 37 °C, 150-200 rpm overnight (18-24 hours).
Collect the culture when adequately cloudy; optimal OD600 is between 2.0 and 2.4.

steps.title: Prepare for Glycerol Stock
steps.instruction: Ensure the culture is in the appropriate growth phase for freezing.

substeps.instruction: Grow the culture until it reaches mid- to late-log phase (typically OD600 of 0.6–1.0).
If the culture was stored at 4 °C, revive it 1:1 with fresh TB and antibiotics at 37 °C, 150-200 rpm for ~1 hour.

steps.title: Create Glycerol Stocks
steps.instruction: Prepare long-term cryopreserved stocks of the bacteria.

substeps.instruction: Label sterile cryovials with strain name, date, plasmid, and antibiotic information.
Pipette 500 µL of well-mixed culture into a labeled cryovial.
Add 500 µL of sterile 50% (v/v) glycerol (1:1 glycerol and sterile water) to reach a final concentration of 25% (v/v).
Mix thoroughly by gentle pipetting; avoid bubbles and inverting.
Immediately freeze the cryovials at -80 °C.

steps.title: Collect Bacterial Pellets
steps.instruction: Harvest bacteria for plasmid extraction or storage.

substeps.instruction: Pellet 1.5 mL of bacterial culture at 6000 rcf (Room Temperature) for 5 minutes in a microcentrifuge tube.
Discard supernatant and repeat until all bacteria are collected.
Adjust centrifugation if needed: increase to 6,000 x g for 10 mins if pellet is loose, or reduce to 4,000 x g for 5-10 mins if pellet is too tight.
Proceed immediately to plasmid extraction, or store pellets at -20 °C (short-term) or -80 °C (long-term). For -80 °C storage, remove as much supernatant as possible or snap-freeze in liquid nitrogen.

steps.title: Revive from Glycerol Stock
steps.instruction: Recover bacteria from a frozen stock for new inoculation.

substeps.instruction: Retrieve the glycerol stock from -80 °C and keep on ice.
Using a sterile tip, remove a small speck of frozen stock from the surface.
Inoculate the speck directly into 1 mL of antibiotic-free TB in a sterile tube.
Incubate at 37 °C, 150-200 rpm for 1 hour.
Continue inoculation by adding additional TB and appropriate antibiotics to reach a final volume of 3-7 mL for overnight culture.
